entries.hypothesis: The lower-radio result selected by event 0x102f is 0x0fc3
entries.conclusion: The event branch loads 0x0fbf at 0x24788e and enters the dispatcher call at 0x246ad6 with that value intact; swap16-aware table decoding maps it to 0x245cb2 -> 0x253610

entries.hypothesis: Lower result 0x0fbf selects 0x245c76 -> 0x2525a8 -> task-10 0x1392 and completes task 17
entries.conclusion: The result table maps 0x0fbf to context handler 0x253610, 0x0fc1 to completion status 0x1391, and 0x0fc2 to radio-state status 0x1392; only the 0x1391 task-10 route can reach 0x0434

entries.hypothesis: Forcing numeric event 0x05e8 proves the organic registration predecessor
entries.conclusion: The event is a valid argumentless callback input, but forcing it bypasses the unresolved publisher activation and downstream readiness path

entries.hypothesis: A DSP type-0x80 primitive-0x70 response completes the current registration context
entries.conclusion: The real RX path delivers the fabricated primitive-0x70 payload, but task 13 rejects it across tested delays; this disproves that payload only, not the broader type-0x80 family decoded at 0x284ac4

entries.hypothesis: A valid type-0x80/type-0x83 0x040b transfer supplies the missing ordinary-registration 0x05dc/0x05e8 predecessor
entries.conclusion: Successful task-13 segmented-transfer reassembly at 0x23e62c emits task-16 status 0x05eb; callback 0x3c handles it on a dedicated branch that publishes 0x057a and returns 0x05e6, bypassing its 0x05e8 fallback and constructing no object-bearing 0x05dc lifecycle. The task-13 subsystem is not yet identified; it must not be conflated with the task-6 UI window stack

entries.hypothesis: A validated DSP RX packet family populates the task-21 0x120c/D0 object path
entries.conclusion: That path is GSM 11.14 SIM Toolkit: TERMINAL PROFILE/91xx -> 0x120c -> FETCH A0/12 -> proactive D0 command. Validated DSP RX families have no edge into this SAT chain; this does not exclude a different DSP-owned registration path

entries.hypothesis: Periodic header-only DSP RX type-0x03 liveness traffic activates the missing ordinary-registration publisher
entries.conclusion: Two independent empty-ring-gated DSP RAM/FIQ0 runs were consumed by task 4. The first incremented firmware activity counter 0x112502 but emitted none of 0x05e8, 0x05ea, 0x07dd, 0x09d8, or 0x0434. The later 182-heartbeat experiment also emitted none of callback-0x1a status 0x1400, initializer status 0x08ac, controller status 0x0795, or report code 7. A newer coherent profile reaches 0x08ac through a different controller owner; this does not change the finding that liveness traffic alone supplies no semantic completion

entries.hypothesis: The organic outbound DSP type-0x70 payload 0a 09 expects a type-0x74 echo which completes task 13 and reports startup code 7
entries.conclusion: An empty-ring-gated type-0x74 payload 0a 09 was delivered through the real DSP RX/FIQ0 path and produced no task-13 message, 0x05eb, code 7, or mode advance. The later owner census closes the premise statically: handler 0x234954 posts 0a09 only after it has consumed the correlated type-0x74/0d00 completion, making 0a09 a one-way post-completion publication rather than another request.

entries.hypothesis: An ordinary DSP-downstream completion advances callback-state slot 0x45 and selects 0x09d0 as the missing report-code-7 predecessor
entries.conclusion: Runtime observes only zero writes. Static coverage comprises 46 selector-0x45 catalogue rows (all state 0x3f/preserve), all 46 generic initialization/reconciliation records (no selector 0x45), 47 exact-address literal references (one direct store, the global-0x05e2 reset at 0x299ba0), and 57 array-base literal references (broad indexed writers only clear the slot). No identified writer reaches a DSP prerequisite. The 0x09d0 path remains mapped but has no evidenced ordinary owner.

entries.hypothesis: A normal 3210 ADC value or calibration activates one of the two power-owned report-code-7 callers during ordinary boot
entries.conclusion: The 0x21e40c caller is battery event 0x25 under the firmware string 'Check voltage level for shutdown'. Predicate 0x27cd82 returns one above the shutdown threshold and skips the reporter; only the at-or-below result reaches it. Selector 1 value 0x1b0 powers off before task 1, while 0x1c0 reaches mode 0x0004 with battery band 2 and no code 7. The 0x21f8de caller is power state 0x0c, labelled 'CHARGING COMPLETED', and reports after event 0x42. The coherent no-charger run instead follows 0x1a -> 0x1c -> 0x05 -> 0x04 and receives event 0x42 in state 0x04 without transitioning. These are shutdown/charging outcomes, not the missing ordinary-ready producer

entries.hypothesis: The selector-4=0x14 detour reaches an unfinished normal task-19 pack-characterization state whose completion supplies report code 7
entries.conclusion: Static correction shows low selector 4 is not intrinsically abnormal: below 39 selects init mode 4, and the independent consumer below 26 clears charge/fault state 0 and posts event 0x44. Mode 4 skips the 0x27d5fc source-7 guard, but its distinct completion state waits for event 0x43. A single statically derived fixture (selector 4=0x14, selector 1=0x180) selects mode 4 without poweroff but leaves the monitor uninitialized, checklist 0x0b, task 1 in mode 0x000d, and code 7 absent. Backward census proves the sole event-0x43 poster is selected by payload 3 of incoming class-`0x40` service command 0x8e; the handler's sole MCU 0x8e construction is its acknowledgement. This is a dormant external service/test request, not an ordinary battery completion, so neither event 0x43 nor mode 4 is a valid normal-boot escape.

entries.hypothesis: Callback-table index 0x1a receives an ordinary-boot callback return 0x1400 and initiates the 0x08ac to 0x0795 code-7 chain
entries.conclusion: 0x1400 is decoded from an argumentless task-5 mailbox message at 0x2af57c, not returned by a callback. All 188 direct task-5 event-helper calls have recovered constant events and none emits 0x1400; the remaining unresolved-destination sender routes through a service table that does not target task 5. The chain is a mapped dormant or service-specific contract, not the strongest ordinary-boot route

entries.hypothesis: Display statuses 0x0280, 0x0281, or 0x0282 head the ordinary-boot lifecycle that supplies global 0x05eb and report code 7
entries.conclusion: The 0x028x states are owned by the transaction engine around 0x264504/0x264c98 and reached from class-`0x40` service commands 0x81/0x82 and local/test ASCII command frontends. No catalogue or literal producer establishes an ordinary source, and coherent controller-transform tracing produces none of them. The route is valid but service/test-specific.

entries.hypothesis: Display status 0x06ca supplies ordinary report code 7 through 0x0795 while task 1 is parked in mode 0x0004
entries.conclusion: The 0x06ca case at 0x28c268 reaches the 0x0795 generator only when getter 0x2af066 returns startup/display state 7. The coherently observed mode-0x0004 route establishes state 3 through setter 0x2af058; state 7 belongs a separate mode-2 branch after input code 0x10. Coherent runtime observes state 3 and no 0x06ca/0x0795 publication.

entries.hypothesis: The organically reached 0x08ac -> 0x27f150 controller route is the unconditional ordinary-boot owner of 0x0795 and task-1 report code 7
entries.conclusion: The corrected guard is 0x11fd04, but coherent service-5 initialization proves initializer 0x27f9e8 owns it from EF_ACMmax. A standards-valid exhausted account reaches 0x27f23e organically and the function publishes 0x019a, not 0x0795. The true non-display 0x0795 producer at 0x28796a is reached after 0x08b0. The variable-length catalogue proves two inputs: packed 0x213a/0x613a expands to 0x089a,0x08b0 and packed 0x213b/0x613b emits 0x08b0 directly. Status 0x013a is consumed by callback 0x24 in framework mode 11; callback 0x013b is registered only after input 0x03ab establishes the same later mode, while coherent startup remains in mode 0. The other literal producer requires display state 7. Thus 0x08ac -> 0x27f150 is not the ordinary code-7 route.

entries.hypothesis: The organic outbound DSP type-0x1a packet is a request whose direct inbound reply supplies task-17 registration completion
entries.conclusion: The sole caller of builder 0x219f0c is task-10 state dispatcher 0x21ba54; after posting the packet the builder retains no transaction token, reply object, or task-3 callback, arms only the global DSP cadence timer, clears the activity counter, and returns after task 17 has already received 0x043c. Full builder decode identifies the payload as a 503-position GSM 900/DCS 1800 ARFCN bitmap; the coherent offline source is rejected by its density guard and publishes a zero channel set with flag 0x81. The apparent type-0x80 correlation at 0x284c74 instead tests radio-controller state 0x10dbd2, observed as 0x00 at the send, against later state 0x1a and can publish 0x1395 rather than 0x1391. Type 0x1a is a fire-and-forget channel-set publication, not the missing direct registration request

entries.hypothesis: The task-21 0x120c -> A0/12 -> D0 path is the missing ordinary SIM-registration predecessor
entries.conclusion: A0/12 and D0 are the GSM 11.14 FETCH/proactive-command protocol. Firmware arms it only after TERMINAL PROFILE for phase >=3, and the profile-download function belongs to a later session lifecycle

entries.hypothesis: Controller modes 0x11 and 0x13 select non-SAT callbacks 0x3a and 0x36 that can activate ordinary registration through 0x0578
entries.conclusion: Exhaustive concrete execution of dispatcher 0x253e20 maps mode 0x11 only from event 0x1782 and mode 0x13 only from event 0x1779; the complete mode map is sourced exclusively by the proactive-SIM 0x1770..0x1788 family

entries.hypothesis: Task-15 status 0x09ee is an independent lower-peer result which starts the callback-7 session factory
entries.conclusion: Seven branches inside task 15 construct 0x09ee through 0x208ee0; task 15 forwards its local result to task 17, which constructs 0x0a2e and returns it before the factory runs. The absent predecessor is the earlier object-bearing task-15 operation, not 0x09ee or 0x0a2e

entries.hypothesis: A valid DSP type-0x80 segmented completion correlated with the organic type-0x70 0a09 transaction supplies callback 0x5d status 0x05eb and report code 7
entries.conclusion: The packet traverses FIQ0, normalizes to 0x040b, returns parser result 0x061a, and publishes 0x05eb directly to task 16 through 0x23e1a4. It does not enter the global callback sweep, call the code-7 reporter, or advance task 1 beyond mode 0x0004

entries.hypothesis: Callback 0x47's shared 0x05e1 branch is selected by absent dynamic statuses 0x0778 and 0x1441
entries.conclusion: Correct subtract-cascade execution yields 0x0578 and 0x1440. The observed 0x05dc branch starts the generic text/UI manager through 0x24b174 -> 0x24af70, stores 0x0578 as its completion, and publishes 0x057c when presented. The coherent run reaches 0x05dc/0x057c but no interactive completion. This is not an absent DSP/network reply or the unconditional code-7 owner.

entries.hypothesis: A valid phone identity/security profile completes callback 0x47 through 0x0578 -> 0x05e1 -> 0x06c5 and supplies startup report code 7
entries.conclusion: The default combined EEPROM checksums were already valid. A firmware-derived fixture supplies a synthetic IMEI, default phone code 12345, and matching derived record at 0x06c8. The 0x2ae61a comparison succeeds at 0x0317, callback 0x47 is not selected, and the Security-code prompt becomes the idle Menu frame. A later physical left-softkey fixture proves that frame is interactive and opens Phone book while task 1 remains in mode 0x0004. No 0x05e1, 0x06c5, code 7, or mode exit is required. Security provisioning controls the prompt but does not own code 7.

entries.hypothesis: Inbound ROM-4 DSP group/class 0x74 payload 0x13 00 is the missing code-7 completion
entries.conclusion: In this ROM first-level class 0x74 reaches 0x234954. Its recognized contact/self-test completion payload is 0x0d 00 and clears the contact busy flag at 0x2349dc. Payload 0x13 00 falls through the generic path and has no static route to 0x05e1, 0x05eb, 0x06c5, or any code-7 reporter. Group labels from another decoder layer cannot be replayed as this class byte.

entries.hypothesis: The organic post-SIM 0x05e1 is a global completion that reaches callback 0x5d and supplies report code 7
entries.conclusion: In both unprovisioned and provisioned coherent runs, the observed startup 0x05e1 is delivered specifically to selected callback 0x2f, whose initialization lifecycle expects 0x05e0/0x05e1. A new negative control enters wrong phone code 11111 through the physical keypad: verifier mismatch makes callback 0x47 publish 0x05e1, but the dispatcher selects callback 0x47 again and never callback 0x5d. Callback 0x5d receives only its early 0x05e2 initialization. The later repeating 0x0d16 is independently decoded as task-5 timer class 0x3d, rearmed by the resource-0x62 periodic poll, and is not a completion. Status values are callback-scoped, not global broadcasts.

entries.hypothesis: Callback 0x47's accepted-code result 0x05e6 reaches a missing display/DSP completion boundary that should select the idle window
entries.conclusion: The generic callback dispatcher handles 0x05e6 explicitly at 0x2ac54c by advancing its callback cursor. Task 6 later receives class-2 and class-3 editor-lifecycle messages, but no class-1 idle-window selection follows: control byte 0x1116fd never arms the 0x2a255c idle helper, resource 0x4c22 and event 0x0547 are absent, and no DSP TX is constructed. The accepted editor transaction closes within firmware and is not blocked on display hardware.

entries.hypothesis: Supplying report code 7 in isolation creates a coherent MMI/display lifecycle whose later completion identifies the faithful missing boundary
entries.conclusion: The isolated report enters the conditional mode-4 continuation: firmware posts 0x0732 to task 5, initializes task 6, and task 6 posts 0x0547. It does not compose. The forced path runs while task 5 retains its existing backlog; the 0x0547 object remains queued while internal timer traffic wins the receive path. Later consumer-side decode proved that ordinary interactive initialization already falls through without code 7, and physical power input identifies code 7 as a shutdown continuation. Neither the report nor its downstream statuses should be injected.

entries.hypothesis: A healthy 3210 starts task 6 or posts 0x0732 through an ordinary entrance independent of task 1's code-7 branches
entries.conclusion: The exhaustive effective-literal inventory contains four 0x0732 sites. Three populate event fields or registration structures. The sole direct publisher is 0x2a26d4, whose only callers are 0x270f7a and 0x271292 immediately after the two explicit task-1 code-7 receives. Task 6's idle-window helper is reachable only from its own receive loop after startup. No independent ordinary entrance is present in this statically enumerable surface.

entries.hypothesis: A missing or insufficiently held PWRONX interrupt prevents the ordinary power-on completion from publishing report code 7
entries.conclusion: MAD2 IRQ line 0 is enabled and acknowledged through 0x2b3084. Its handler calls 0x2b4662, which posts event 0x41 to task 1 for the early power-key scan. Holding the emulated key raises 51 interrupts in a bounded run, but callback 0x5d still receives only 0x05e2, code 7 remains absent, and task 1 stays in mode 0x0004. Task 19's separate numeric event-0x41 branch is labelled CHARGER CONNECTION and has no producer edge from this IRQ.

entries.hypothesis: The contact/DSP self-test verdict remains incomplete and suppresses the ordinary code-7 publication
entries.conclusion: Firmware organically constructs contact flags 0xc8. The modeled request-derived RX class-0x74 payload 0d00 reaches 0x2349c8 and clears pending bit 2, after which task 5 consumes ready bit 7 at 0x29bc8c and leaves steady flags 0x49. The self-test completion and ready-bit lifecycle therefore complete normally; the associated immediate event 0x1a is a kernel completion, not a task-1 report.

entries.hypothesis: Injected 0x1196 or replayed commit keys can establish coherent SIM registration
entries.conclusion: They reach downstream handlers without the owned reply object and never set ENABLE organically

entries.hypothesis: Task-8 0x8d/0x8e traffic is the missing generic-service peer response
entries.conclusion: No evidenced edge links this traffic to an organic 0x05e8 publisher path

entries.hypothesis: Scheduler event 0x74 producers also produce class-`0x40` service command 0x74
entries.conclusion: They are separate namespaces and transports; the command is an external request with an MCU acknowledgement

entries.hypothesis: The deep-profile command-0x64 storm is repeated watchdog result 2 or repeated consumption of the injected response allocation
entries.conclusion: The injected result-5 allocation is consumed and freed once. Firmware-generated status frames then pass through task 7 with route selector 1 and return as fresh task-2 allocations, repeatedly re-entering 0x236dc4 with result 5. The anomaly is caused by the provisional responder's incomplete transport session, not the watchdog

entries.hypothesis: Report code 7 is a generic ROM-4 DSP/startup completion and a healthy sibling boot can supply a replayable peer contract
entries.conclusion: NSE-1 v5.30 contains the exact report-7 wrapper at 0x28f142 and exactly four callers at 0x22cb7e, 0x22dc62, 0x246eaa, and 0x26af8a. A forcing-free 60-million-instruction sibling boot reaches its byte-exact interactive Security-code frame without executing the wrapper. The 5110 uses a serial-keypad scan lifecycle and its wrapper only posts code 7; the 3210 wrapper additionally publishes resource 0x6a01 readiness. This disproves a generic ROM-4/DSP completion and agrees with the later 3210 result that code 7 belongs to conditional power/shutdown continuation rather than ordinary boot.

entries.hypothesis: A faithful 3210 ADC routing and factory calibration fixture can hold one constant source-7 value that survives cold boot, produces classifier state 3, and advances 0x2a6942
entries.conclusion: Both cold-boot safety 0x27d5fc and the later classifier consume source 7, which runtime maps to physical CCONT channel 1, through the same gain, zero offset, and 1500/313 scaling. Cold boot powers off below 0x0834, while state 3 requires a value below 0x076c. These ranges are disjoint by 200 scaled units for every common affine calibration. At unity gain the predicted minimum safe raw value is 0x1b7 and the maximum state-3 value is 0x18c; coherent runs confirm 0x1b6 powers off before task 1 and 0x1b7 reaches mode 0x000d. EEPROM descriptors 2/3/4 map to 0x0248..0x025b; both collected 3210 images are erased there and validly select ROM defaults. No safe constant-input fixture reached state 3 or a legitimate code-7 caller.

entries.hypothesis: Reader 0x2a68c4 and helpers 0x2b64fc/0x2b59e0/0x2b5446/0x2b63cc interpolate a selector-1/selector-4 pair into a recognized-pack class that can supply an ordinary fixture
entries.conclusion: The complete 0x2a68c4 path reads selector 1 once and applies scalar integer-to-float, division by coefficient [0x11fde0+0x34], multiplication by coefficient [0x11fde0+0x38], and float-to-integer conversion. Selector 4 is handled independently by 0x2b4f2c using one raw threshold: below 39 stores 0x141 and selects init mode 4; otherwise it stores 0x4fb and selects mode 1. All 11 selector-1 reader callers, all five selector-4 decision callers, the sole 0x27cbec caller, and the sole recovered event-0x43 poster were classified. No two-input table or unique recognized region exists in this surface, so no non-swept coherent fixture can be derived from it.

entries.hypothesis: The proper mode-0d advance requires monitor state 3, making the safe mode-1 guard and later gate statically disjoint
entries.conclusion: Exhaustive decode of 0x2a6942 proves state 0 returns 2, states 1/2 return 0, state 3 returns 1 or 3 according to flag bit 5, and every other byte returns 2. The mode-0d caller at 0x270edc accepts every nonzero result. Writer coverage shows 0x27ddfa initializes 0x110436 to state 0 and the sole later writer 0x27dcfa stores classifier states 1/2/3; no initialized writer produces state 4. Coherent runtime reaches the gate after state 1 has been published, but the accepted pre-classification state 0 removes the claimed static contradiction and points to readiness-versus-monitor ordering instead of an impossible ADC value.

entries.hypothesis: Completing the application-readiness checklist before the first battery classification selects the accepted mode-0d branch and removes the code-7 boot wall
entries.conclusion: The full checklist is delayed as one firmware task group behind completion of the modeled service-empty 0x622a transaction. The serialized type-0x05 report is one-way; completion uses the separate DSPIF shared-control path, not an RX packet acknowledgement. Task 18 is merely the last task in the fixed resume order and posts code 0x12 immediately from its initializer. Shortening the peer's calibrated delay could change which tail 0x2a6942 selects, but both tails compare a mailbox report before falling through to equivalent interactive initialization. Timing changes the recorded continuation, not whether the UI starts; no timing constant was changed.

entries.hypothesis: The current single-timer DSP peer can schedule all modeled service-transport ring and shared-control completions solely from retained DSPIF command-4 doorbells
entries.conclusion: Independent service-transport ring and shared-service timers reproduce the coherent profile. A doorbell-only run leaves task 1 in mode 0x000d with service-session status 0x0089 and SIM disabled because command 4 does not accompany every ring commit. The observed ring-producer and service-pending scheduling edges remain required; DSPIF command 4 is real but is not a universal trigger for both protocols.

entries.hypothesis: The adjacent status-0x0794/code-6 and status-0x0795/code-7 routes form the missing ordinary bootstrap lifecycle
entries.conclusion: The pair is structurally real but has no evidenced ordinary initiator. Status 0x0794 selects 0x28c22c and code 6, but its sole predecessor is packed catalogue input 0x32b4/0x72b4, neither of which has an in-ROM producer. Both effective 0x0795 producers are later conditional routes. The non-display route requires framework mode 11 established by 0x03ab; 0x03ab has one consumer and no in-ROM producer. Correcting keypad ownership later proved that security-editor input is independent of this pair, so the pair remains excluded as the ordinary keypad/bootstrap owner.

entries.hypothesis: A missing registration or lifecycle transition should select callback 0x01 when the organic physical-key path publishes status 0x0367, completing the ordinary UI-start chain
entries.conclusion: Callback 0x01 is a fixed callback-table entry with zero records in the complete 950-record transition table. The callback engine initializes it and sweeps it organically during startup; by the post-frontier Up event the active callback has advanced elsewhere. Descriptor selector 0x75 is a separate namespace with eleven records and maps state-zero 0x0367 to 0x051d. Thus 0x0367 -> callback 0x01 -> 0x03e9 is a conditional navigation action during callback 0x01's lifecycle, not a missing hardware boundary or the ordinary startup entrance.

entries.hypothesis: An ordinary startup lifecycle should select callback 0x10 and publish 0x05e7, causing the full application/UI initialization sequence
entries.conclusion: Callback 0x10 is a fixed callback-plane entry with zero transition records. The sole recovered global 0x05e7 publisher is 0x256f68, and its complete ROM caller set consists of controller status 0x03e9's conditional navigation route and the already-classified local/service-test statuses 0x0280/0x0281/0x0282. In an unattended coherent run callback 0x10 receives only initialization status 0x05e2; neither 0x256f68 nor the 0x05e7 branch executes. The path is conditional UI reinitialization, not the cold-boot entrance.

entries.hypothesis: Task-5 leaf 0x28c248 and class-1 constructor 0x2b1e44 are the missing ordinary cold-boot entrance to task 6's idle window
entries.conclusion: Concrete execution of all 65,536 inputs to dispatcher 0x28bddc finds exactly one status reaching 0x28c248: 0x0732. Firmware produces 0x0732 organically after a physical power key posts report code 7 and enters mode 0x000c, proving this is conditional power/shutdown UI lifecycle rather than unattended startup. A 20-second trace and a post-security-code run both show task 1 starting shutdown/service teardown before task 5 performs another outer receive; 0x0732 consequently remains queued and no downstream class-1 message, resource 0x4c22, or event 0x0547 executes. This is shutdown ordering, not a missing task-5 queue or hardware acknowledgement.

entries.hypothesis: Repeated status 0x05a7 after a second physical softkey is a post-security UI transaction retry stalled on a missing completion
entries.conclusion: Correct concrete execution shows 0x05a7 reaches dispatcher target 0x28c480 and calls 0x2b3222, a three-slot timer manager. Target 0x28c43c belongs exclusively to status 0x05f3; the former 0x28c43a attribution was mid-instruction. Callback 0x47 settles normally after accepted 0x0578 -> 0x05e6 and leaves the active sweep. A negative-control run with only 12345 plus its single submission reproduces the later post-acceptance event wave. Overlapping 0x00c8 is independently published once per second by task 1 at 0x2a2838 and expands to context-maintenance outputs, not a class-1 window selection. No timer completion or callback result is justified for injection.

entries.hypothesis: 3210 boot requires the fast MHz-range Timer-0 calibration; the recovered 33,055 Hz CTSI rate cannot complete startup
entries.conclusion: Both supported 3210 ROMs boot to the interactive menu with both MAD2 timers at the 33,055 Hz CTSI default. The fast calibration starved task 2's watchdog service, expiring CCONT at exactly 49 seconds, and its apparent necessity came from the invented external-service result-5 transition suspending application tasks when scheduler delays ran at their real rate (see external_service_result5_ordinary_startup)

entries.hypothesis: External-service command 0x64 result 5 is part of ordinary healthy startup and should be transmitted by the peer
entries.conclusion: Result 5 suspends tasks 10..17; the speculative peer transmission suspended task 17 before the later 0x1587 post once timers ran at the real CTSI rate. With that lifecycle removed, both 3210 revisions settle at service-session status 0x49 and reach the interactive menu

entries.hypothesis: Shared-control word 0xe0 must expose value 1 until the periodic service tick so firmware can observe completion in progress
entries.conclusion: A trial exposing 0xe0=1 until the then-5 ms service tick regressed the deep boot. Completion visibility is not a tunable delay; no delay may be calibrated merely to reproduce an oracle

entries.hypothesis: Status 0x13fe advances to 0x0795 as the ordinary frontier transition of one controller lifecycle
entries.conclusion: A standards-valid exhausted-account fixture (ACM == ACMmax == 1) makes 0x27f150 construct its activity slot and take 0x27f23e, which publishes status 0x019a, not 0x0795. The two literal 0x0795 producers require display state 7 or dual-selector unavailability with controller state 2; the join crossed two distinct controller lifecycles

entries.hypothesis: 3210 firmware does not select or read EF_IMSI during SIM initialization
entries.conclusion: The absence was an artifact of a malformed MF/DF GSM-specific SELECT response layout, which also held firmware in a repeating STATUS presence loop. With correct directory metadata (including the 0x15 GSM-data length), firmware organically selects and reads EF_IMSI and leaves the preliminary cycle. Directory metadata must be modeled correctly rather than suppressing the STATUS poll

entries.hypothesis: MAD2 GenIO signal-register bit 6 (0x20020) drives the 3210 LCD/keypad backlight
entries.conclusion: The NSE-8/9 service manual routes both illumination outputs behind COBBA_GJP into the N400 UI-Switch. Paired v5.01/v6.00 traces covering a physical key press plus a 35-second timeout show no change on bit 6 or any candidate PUP/UIF output latch, and a changed-write census of the complete MCU-visible DSP shared window finds no key- or timeout-specific light command. Boot-time 0x20020 bit-3 traffic is the proven EEPROM clock. The MAD2-to-COBBA light command remains unmapped; no backlight state is synthesized
